taxonomic_note: Accepted at species rank. Central Texas material is often treated regionally as var. grandiflora; that name is retained as infraspecific/historical context, not a duplicate learner taxon.
look_here_first: Look at stature and leaves: a tall perennial with narrow linear-lanceolate leaves and a long open flowering axis. Then inspect the green, hairy but non-mealy calyx.
project_tracker_diagnostic: Tall perennial with narrow opposite linear-lanceolate leaves, long open terminal flowering axis, and green ribbed hairy calyces lacking the farinose/mealy coating of S. farinacea.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County native inventory, Travis County preserve/herbarium records, and UT Williamson County treatment; no county presence inferred.

morphology_keys.habit: Perennial from a woody rootstock, often much taller than the low spring sages.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, narrow linear-lanceolate to linear-oblanceolate leaves.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Long terminal interrupted flowering axis with repeated verticils.
morphology_keys.calyx: Green, ribbed and glandular-hairy, not white-mealy/felted.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Mealy blue sage has a conspicuously mealy/felted calyx. Engelmann sage is a low dense clump with strongly glandular foliage and compact flowering architecture.
